text:
sre-oncall: Heads-up — apiserver p95 in eu-west3 just spiked to ~1.2s coincident with a large GPU pool onboarding batch. controller-manager restarted twice in the last 10m. Anyone already looking?
dana: seeing the same. etcd follower RPCs timing out to the leader around the onboarding window. not a clear disk i/o pattern.
jay: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/team/eng-sre/d/EU3/controlplane?orgId=1
sre-oncall: dropping relevant logs: ```E0301 12:03:21 apiserver.go:123] watch handler error: dial tcp 10.2.1.5:2379: i/o timeout
controller-manager: panic: lease renew failed: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc = transport is closing```
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created and page sent to @sre-oncall :rotating_light:
oliver: could this be NAT / conntrack exhaustion from the onboarding burst? eu-west3 NAT porta usage jumped.
dana: confirmed — ephemeral port exhaustion spike aligned with provisioning surge, conntrack entries > 600k for kube-proxy on some nodes.
kevin: we should throttle the rollout. i'd rather cap the provisioner surge than bounce control plane. can someone set max-surge to 2 and pause the scale job?
jay: done — provisioner autoscale cap set to 30 (was 100). paused the onboarding job.
dana: after capping, conntrack started to decline and etcd RPC failures dropped. apiserver p95 back to ~180ms, controller-manager stable.
oliver: follow-ups: 1) add NAT pool / elastic IPs for eu-west3 (cost estimate ~$20k/mo) 2) implement egress proxy so nodes don't exhaust SNAT 3) pre-warm control plane (ephemeral connections) before large onboards.
sre-oncall: agree on all three. also add a precheck in the provisioner to throttle based on conntrack and NAT headroom. create RFC for NAT capacity + prewarm work?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered — gpu-provisioner v2 -> v1 (initiated by dana)
sre-oncall: thanks. monitoring closely for the next 60m. will update INC and spin up a post-mortem if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:
